extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners/appellants (attorneys, agents, and applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and responding to an examiner's answer in a patent appeal, including required contents, conference requirements, new-ground procedures, timing, and substitute answers on remand. Applies to examiners drafting answers and appellants responding to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of examiner's answer (incorporation of grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer to the appeal brief. An examiner's answer is deemed to incorporate all of the grounds of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified by any advisory action and pre-appeal brief conference decision), unless the examiner's answer expressly indicates that a ground of rejection has been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every ground from the Office action is treated as being on appeal and explicitly list any withdrawn rejections under 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS.' If a ground is not argued by appellant or is requested to be held in abeyance, the examiner should maintain the rejection in the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to include a new ground of rejection in the answer
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's answer may include a new ground of rejection. Any rejection that relies upon Evidence not relied upon in the Office action is a new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New grounds must be prominently identified as 'NEW GROUNDS OF REJECTION,' include a complete explanation with references to applicable statutes, prior art, and claim numbers, and must be approved and signed by the Director (delegated to TC Directors or designees). Conclude answers raising new grounds with the required notification of appellant's reply options and TC Director approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's response options to a new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner's answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground, appellant must within two months either (1) request that prosecution be reopened by filing a reply under §1.111 with or without amendment/affidavit/evidence, or (2) request that the appeal be maintained by filing a reply brief under §41.41 addressing each new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply brief may not be accompanied by amendments/affidavits/evidence; if it is, it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution. Extensions under 1.136(a) do not apply to this two-month period (see 1.136(b) for limited extensions). Failure to timely exercise an option may result in sua sponte dismissal of the appeal as to the claims subject to the new ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal conference requirement and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal conference is mandatory in all cases in which an acceptable brief has been filed, unless the examiner and SPE agree the appeal should not go forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should include the examiner preparing the answer, a supervisory patent examiner (SPE), and a conferee examiner with sufficient experience. Consider dropping cumulative rejections and eliminating doubtful technical rejections. The answer must list 'Conferees:' with their typed/printed names and initials; omission may lead the Patent Appeal Center to return the answer for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required order and headings in the examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's answer should include, under appropriate headings and in the indicated order, items such as: Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal; Withdrawn Rejections; New Grounds of Rejection; Response to Argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed headings and follow form paragraph templates (e.g., ¶ 12.254, ¶ 12.255, ¶ 12.256, ¶ 12.257, ¶ 12.261). When restating rejections, use form paragraph 12.255 as needed. New grounds must be prominently identified (form paragraph 12.256).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that every ground of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken is being maintained by the examiner except for those listed under 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grounds were modified by an advisory action or pre-appeal decision, use the modified-statement form (¶ 12.254.02) and identify the modifying action/date. Use form paragraphs to restate or introduce rejections or withdrawals when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn rejections entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the subheading 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS,' the examiner should list any grounds of rejection that are being withdrawn (e.g., those overcome by appellant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify which grounds are not presented for review and provide explanation in bracketed text per form paragraph guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Argument format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner disagrees with each of the appellant's arguments on the issues presented and an explanation of reasons for disagreement. The examiner must use headings and subheadings paralleling the appellant's brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a written answer within 2 months after receipt of the brief. If an issue was fully responded to under 'Grounds of Rejection...' no additional response is required. If the final rejection already fully addresses the brief's arguments, a simplified 'Response to Arguments' referring to the final rejection is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of affidavits/declarations/exhibits filed with or after appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or exhibits filed with the notice of appeal must be treated in accordance with 37 CFR 1.116. If refused entry under 1.116 or prohibited by 41.33, the examiner should not comment; appellant should not rely on non-entered material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant has grounds to challenge non-entry, they should file a timely petition under 1.181. Affidavits swearing behind a reference should be clearly identified as being considered under 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language documents and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document relied upon by the examiner is in a language other than English, a translation must be obtained so the record is clear as to the precise facts relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machine translations or English equivalents are acceptable; see MPEP §2120 for reliance on abstracts and foreign language documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that all pending, rejected claims are on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are not required to determine whether fewer than all rejected claims are identified as being appealed. The Board will presume all rejected claims are on appeal except those canceled by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat all pending, rejected claims as being on appeal and maintain rejections unless appellant has overcome them. If appellant did not argue a rejection or requested it be held in abeyance, identify that the appellant did not argue it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of how final rejection applies to amended/added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where amendments after final action are entered for appeal purposes, the examiner must identify (in an advisory action) how one or more individual rejections set forth in the final rejection would be used to reject the added or amended claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear mapping of prior rejections to amended claims so the record shows how the rejections would apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner reevaluation and withdrawal of unsupported rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should reevaluate their position in light of arguments presented and expressly withdraw any rejections not adhered to in the 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS' subsection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all rejections of an independent claim are withdrawn while others remain, note the change of status. If dependent claims' rejections change, note those changes and advise applicant of options (e.g., rewrite dependent claim in independent form under 41.33(b)(2) before the time in 90.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and signature requirements for new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: New grounds of rejection must be approved by a Technology Center (TC) Director or designee and the answer must include the signature of the TC Director or designee to indicate approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.39 specifies Director approval; authority delegated to TC Directors. For answers containing a new ground, include TC Director signature and use form paragraph 12.279.01 concluding the answer with the required notification of appellant's two-month options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs and prescribed templates
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 12.249 cover sheet; ¶ 12.254 grounds; ¶ 12.255 restatement; ¶ 12.256 new grounds heading; ¶ 12.257 withdrawn rejections; ¶ 12.261 response to argument; ¶ 12.279 conclusions) is provided for use in examiner's answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the examiner notes accompanying each form paragraph for required bracketed insertions, when to use alternate paragraphs, and how to restate or introduce content. Use ¶ 12.279.01 when new grounds are present; use ¶ 12.279 otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of examiner's answer on subsequent procedural time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing date of the examiner's answer begins the period for filing a reply brief (transferring jurisdiction to the Board), the time for appellants to request oral hearing, and the time period for payment of the appeal forwarding fee unless a petition under 1.181 was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's answer is effectively required for an appeal to proceed to the Board under current procedures, even though 37 CFR 41.39(a) uses 'may.' Ensure timely mailing and correct content to avoid jurisdictional/timing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options after examiner considers the appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering the issues on appeal, the examiner may: (A) reopen prosecution to enter a new ground (with SPE approval), (B) allow the application if rejections are overcome, or (C) maintain the appeal by conducting an appeal conference and drafting an examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reopening prosecution is necessary, obtain supervisory approval prior to reopening after an appeal per MPEP §1002.02(d) and §1207.04. If allowing, reasons for allowance may be appropriate to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) for patent applications are not applicable to the time period set forth in this section; see 1.136(b) and 1.550(c) for limited extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept 1.136(a) extension requests for the two-month reply periods to new grounds or substitute answers; advise appellants to consult 1.136(b) or 1.550(c) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning for non-statutory double patenting (NSDP) rejections not argued
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims are rejected on the ground of non-statutory double patenting and the rejection was not addressed in the appeal brief, include a warning (¶ 12.278) explaining that the appeal may be dismissed by a court or the Court may summarily affirm the NSDP rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracketed text, insert the claim numbers subject to NSDP. Explain jurisdictional risks and the need for a terminal disclaimer prior to judicial review if the rejection is not overcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal procedure for failure to reply to new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 41.39(b), if appellant fails to timely file a reply (either request to reopen prosecution or a reply brief addressing new grounds) within two months from the examiner's answer, the appeal as to the claims subject to the new ground is dismissed and those claims may be canceled; remaining claims continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert mailing date and claim numbers in the dismissal form paragraph (¶ 12.279.02). Forward the application to the Board after mailing the dismissal communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute examiner's answer on remand (further consideration of a rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may furnish a substitute examiner's answer in response to a remand by the Board for further consideration of a rejection (37 CFR 41.50(a)). Appellant must within two months either request reopening (reply under 1.111) or maintain the appeal (reply brief under 41.41) to avoid dismissal of the appeal as to the remanded claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute examiner's answer may set forth a new ground of rejection subject to the same TC Director approval requirements. Use form paragraph 12.285 for substitute answers on remand and include reasons supporting the rejections. TC Director must approve substitute answers setting new grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's reply requirements to a substitute examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant requests reopening, the reply under 37 CFR 1.111 must address each ground set forth in the substitute answer within two months and may include amendments/evidence. If appellant requests maintaining the appeal, the reply brief must comply with 41.37(c)(1)(iv) and 41.41 and cannot include new amendments/affidavits/evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply is not fully responsive but is bona fide, the examiner should provide an opportunity to complete the reply under 1.135(c). If not bona fide and two-month period expires, the examiner must sua sponte dismiss the appeal as to the remanded claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute examiner's answer responding to remand not for further consideration of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board remands for reasons other than further consideration of a rejection (e.g., to consider IDS filed while Board had jurisdiction, reply brief raising new issues, amendment, affidavit), the examiner may provide a substitute answer and appellant may file a reply brief within two months. Appellant does not have the option to reopen prosecution unless remand was for further consideration of a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat remands that are not under 41.50(a) differently; provide opportunity to file reply brief but do not accept 1.111 reopening requests in these situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to pay appeal forwarding fee
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to avoid dismissal of the appeal, 37 CFR 41.45 requires payment of an appeal forwarding fee within the time permitted by 41.45(a), unless the fee for filing a brief required by 41.20(b) was timely paid (as of March 18, 2013 reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reminder of appeal forwarding fee requirement in the conclusion paragraph of the examiner's answer (form paragraphs ¶ 12.279 or ¶ 12.279.01). Insert correspondence address of record and initials/signatures where required.
